Reliability and the Write-Ahead Log

Write-ahead logging is a standard method for ensuring data integrity in PostgreSQL.

Changes to data files are written only after those changes have been logged to permanent storage.

After a crash, PostgreSQL recovers the database by replaying the log records.

Because data pages need not be flushed on every commit, WAL reduces the number of disk writes.

Checkpoints mark points in the log where all data files have been updated.
